clue.text: Points out ripe possibilities of advancement

annotationWithheld.clue: Points out ripe possibilities of advancement

clue.text: Various pages lead us to a famous horse

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the word pages come in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jumble of pages somehow leads us to a celebrated horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' makes PEGAS from PAGES; 'lead ... to' just joins it to US.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the winged steed of Greek myth, ridden by Bellerophon.

clue.text: Curse unwilling student dropping out

indicators.note: a student dropping out leaves, so the letter standing for the student is removed

parts.note: loath means unwilling or reluctant
L is the learner plate letter, a common crossword student

explanation.surface: A reluctant student swears as they quit their course.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse can be a swear word, the same sense as a profane oath.

clue.text: Where the stage is set for an operation

explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is where a stage is set for drama; an operating room in a hospital is also called by this name.

clue.text: It is intended to-encourage laying in a little money

explanation.definitionFit: A china egg left in a nest coaxes hens to lay there; the phrase also means modest savings put by.

clue.text: Sweet bird's note cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a tweet is the chirp of a small bird

explanation.surface: A songbird's call, clipped, sounds rather sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means affectedly sweet or quaint, a chiefly British word.

clue.text: I've cut tips for salad

indicators.note: the letters of I've cut into the word for tips, sitting inside it

parts.note: tips are ends
the contraction gives its letters IVE without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone has trimmed the tips of the leaves for a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy chicory plant used as a salad vegetable.

clue.text: It meant no discharge for the old gunner

definitions.text: It meant no discharge for the old gunner

parts.words: It meant no discharge for the old gunner
parts.note: in a flintlock musket, powder could flare in the priming pan without firing the main charge, so the gun failed to go off

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase now means a showy effort that comes to nothing, from a musket's priming powder igniting uselessly.

clue.text: Take it easy! Don't commit suicide

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is advice to relax and avoid strain, and read literally it urges someone not to end their own life.

clue.text: In general exit, one left something

indicators.note: in places the word for exit inside the name of the general

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a gate is a way out

explanation.surface: During a general's departure, someone leaves something behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One left something' reads as someone forgetting an item; in fact it is the one to whom something was left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a beneficiary who receives a bequest under a will.

clue.text: Drug found at college put one's foot down

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A drug discovered at university made someone take a firm stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' suggests being firm; here it means pressing the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: To put one's foot down on the accelerator is to drive faster.

clue.text: Southern timber used in window construction

parts.note: ash is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: Wood from the south is used to build windows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the frame holding glass panes, as in a sliding sash window.

clue.text: Bearing the right number

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's bearing is exactly the right figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that numbs: an old anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, a substance that deadens feeling.

clue.text: Finished and left

explanation.definitionFit: Something done and ended is said to be at an end this way; food left over is remaining.

clue.text: Go up in public transport intended to take in others

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the word for public transport

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word go is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Board a bus that's meant to pick up other passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like giving passengers a ride; it means to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake, made to fool or deceive people.

clue.text: She's the making of Ian

indicators.note: the making suggests the letters of 'of Ian' are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A woman is the person who made Ian what he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a woman's given name, so it fits a female pronoun.

clue.text: Not far out in marine navigation

definitions.text: Not far out in marine navigation

parts.words: Not far out in marine navigation
parts.note: a sailing term for a position or course close to the coast rather than out at sea

explanation.definitionFit: Inshore describes waters or movement near the coast, as opposed to offshore.

clue.text: Dispute the profit, for example

parts.note: a gain is a profit
say is used to mean for example

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the profit, giving an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict a statement.

clue.text: Finished, being nothing less than painstaking

indicators.note: less means the letter for nothing is taken away

parts.note: thorough means painstaking, careful in every detail
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Done, being no less than meticulous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing less than' reads as an intensifier; it tells you to take O away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being through with something means having completed it.

clue.text: Copy original recipe, cooking plaice

indicators.note: original points to the first letter of the word recipe
cooking suggests the fish is prepared, its letters stirred about

explanation.surface: Copy the original recipe while cooking a plaice, a flat fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' looks like part of a kitchen scene, but it signals the anagram of the fish's letters, which follow the R from 'original recipe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of something.

clue.text: She takes after her father?

parts.note: 'takes after' reads as resembling a parent, but here it means inheriting from him once he is gone

explanation.definitionFit: A daughter who inherits her father's estate is his female successor.

clue.text: A nut one adjusts in the back of an open car

definitions.text: the back of an open car

indicators.note: adjusts suggests a mechanic rearranging, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A mechanic tightens a nut in the rear of a convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusts' turns A NUT ONE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau is the rear passenger section of an open motor car.

clue.text: Unusually thin I am getting Vitamin B

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of thin I am appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone unusually thin starts taking a vitamin supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamin is vitamin B1, whose lack causes beriberi.

clue.text: Fickle boy about to betray one's trust

indicators.note: about means the boy's name goes around the word for betraying

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
to rat on someone is to betray them

explanation.surface: An inconstant lad is about to let his friend down.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable and inconsistent in behaviour.

clue.text: Yes, about to include parking spot

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters take in the parking letter
about suggests the letters of yes turned around and moved

parts.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Someone says yes, about to take a parking space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns YES into ESY; 'to include' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it.

clue.text: A book-end

parts.note: not a shelf support but the word printed at the close of a volume

explanation.definitionFit: Finis, Latin for the end, is printed at the close of a book.

clue.text: Statue in the rose-bed

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie within the words the rose-bed

explanation.surface: A statue stands in the middle of the flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across thE ROSe-bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the winged statue at Piccadilly Circus in London.

clue.text: Best sort of capital investment

parts.note: capital is the head and investment is clothing, so this is the finest thing a head can wear

explanation.definitionFit: A halo is the ring of light shown around a saint's head.

clue.text: Collect one's pay with a minor rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word is read upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: a ward is a minor in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: Someone picks up their wages along with a small pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor rise' looks like a small raise in pay; it is a WARD going up.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw one's salary is to receive or collect it.

clue.text: Stir it in a football crowd

indicators.note: in puts the word it inside the crowd

parts.note: a gate is the attendance at a football match

explanation.surface: Stir things up within the crowd at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football, the gate is the number of spectators at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir or shake something, such as a liquid.

clue.text: Master takes female, fifty, in marriage

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
Rita is a female name
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A master marries a woman aged fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to wedlock, as in marital vows.

clue.text: Writer goes to town for a snack

parts.note: Francis Bacon was an English essayist and philosopher
Sandwich is a town in Kent, in south-east England

explanation.surface: An author travels to a town to get a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher sandwich is a popular quick meal of cured pork in bread.
